brief: A narrow two-storey brick commercial front with a stone ground floor, a corbelled parapet and bunting on the windows, a shop door on the corner. One photo. Older than 1970: Lake Erie island and harbour-town main streets (the Put-in-Bay model) are 19th-century commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the Erie County Banking Co. building (Vermilion OH, 1890s-1910s): a two-storey buff-brick bank with stone trim and the bank's name in the parapet, now the city offices; a window air conditioner, flag bunting, a flower box

why.note: a small-town bank turned city hall
